title: Systematic functional, genomic, and safety evaluation of food-derived anti-human norovirus candidate Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus YQ001

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the probiotic properties and safety of Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus YQ001, a yogurt-derived strain previously reported to bind GII.4 human norovirus (HuNoV) and inhibit viral replication in zebrafish larvae.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study evaluated the in vitro probiotic properties and preliminary safety of Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus YQ001, along with its whole-genome analysis, without specifying a particular study design or population.
analysis.methods: The probiotic properties of Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus YQ001 were assessed through in vitro tests, including acid and bile tolerance, auto-aggregation, and radical-scavenging activities. Whole-genome analysis was conducted to compare its genetic characteristics with other strains.
analysis.main_results: Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus YQ001 showed acid and bile tolerance, retaining approximately 30% survival after 3 h at pH 2.0 and over 40% after 4 h in 0.2% bile salts. During sequential simulated gastrointestinal digestion, it retained 35.98% survival after the gastric phase and 45.06% after the intestinal phase. It also showed over 90% auto-aggregation at 24 h and exhibited DPPH and ABTS radical-scavenging activities of 85.17% and 76.35%, respectively.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The phenotypic and genomic findings suggest that Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus YQ001 has potential as a probiotic, although further strain-specific functional and safety evaluation is needed.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide preliminary support for the use of Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus YQ001 as a probiotic candidate for norovirus infection, potentially informing future research and development in this area.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro evaluations and does not include clinical or in vivo testing, which may affect the generalizability of the findings. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the lack of comprehensive safety and efficacy data.

analysis.summary_en: This study systematically evaluated the probiotic properties and safety of Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus YQ001, a yogurt-derived strain previously reported to bind GII.4 human norovirus (HuNoV) and inhibit viral replication in zebrafish larvae. The in vitro tests demonstrated its acid and bile tolerance, auto-aggregation, and radical-scavenging activities. Whole-genome analysis revealed its genetic similarity to other Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus strains. The findings suggest potential probiotic use for norovirus infection, though further strain-specific functional and safety evaluation is required. The study's limitations include reliance on in vitro data and lack of clinical testing, which may affect the generalizability of the results.

title: Prevalence and genotype distribution of norovirus and rotavirus among children under five with diarrheal infection in lower-middle-income countries after Rotavirus vaccine introduction: A systematic review and meta-analysis

analysis.scope_and_question: Background Rotavirus and norovirus are the leading viral causes of acute diarrheal disease worldwide. The study aimed to synthesizes available evidence on the prevalence and genotype distribution of norovirus and rotavirus in children under five years of age in lower-middle-income countries (LMICs) after the introduction of rotavirus vaccination.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: Methods A systematic literature search was conducted across five major databases PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect, Embase, and Web of Science between February 20 and 28, 2026. Duplicate removal, title and abstract screening, full-text review and data extraction were performed independently by two investigators using the Rayyan web-based platform. STATA version 17 software was used for statistical analysis. A random-effects model was applied to estimate pooled prevalence and effect sizes. Heterogeneity was evaluated using Cochran’s Q statistic, the I 2 statistic, forest plots, and Galbraith plots. Publication bias was assessed using both graphical (funnel plots) and statistical methods.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Results A total of 35,704 children under five years with diarrheal infection from LMICs were included across eligible studies. The overall pooled prevalence of norovirus and rotavirus combined was 18% (95% CI: 15–21%). Rotavirus had a higher pooled prevalence than norovirus, at 24% (95% CI: 19.6–28.3%) and 13% (95% CI: 11–15%), respectively. GII, particularly subgenotype GII.4, was the dominant norovirus strain, while G3[P8] and G1[P8] were the most prevalent rotavirus genotypes. Conclusions Norovirus and rotavirus remain significant causes of diarrheal disease among children under five in LMICs, even after the introduction of rotavirus vaccination.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Limitations Substantial heterogeneity was observed across studies (I 2 = 98.72%, p < 0.001). The supplied evidence does not report specific details on the geographic distribution of genotypes or the impact of genotype shifts on vaccine effectiveness.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Implications These findings underscore the need to strengthen surveillance systems, consider circulating genotypes in vaccine formulation, and continuously monitor genotype shifts within the population.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigated the prevalence and genotype distribution of norovirus and rotavirus among children under five with diarrheal infection in lower-middle-income countries (LMICs) following the introduction of rotavirus vaccination. The study included 35,704 children and found that norovirus and rotavirus combined accounted for 18% of diarrheal cases, with rotavirus being more prevalent at 24% and norovirus at 13%. GII.4 was the dominant norovirus strain, while G3[P8] and G1[P8] were the most common rotavirus genotypes. The review highlights the importance of monitoring genotype shifts and improving surveillance systems to address the ongoing burden of these viruses. The analysis also noted substantial heterogeneity across studies, indicating the need for more detailed regional and genetic studies.

title: Molecular Prevalence and Determinants of Adenovirus and Norovirus Among Diarrhoeic Children in Ilorin Metropolis, Kwara State, Nigeria

analysis.research_question_and_background: Viral gastroenteritis remains a major public health concern and a leading cause of morbidity among children under five worldwide. Adenovirus (Adv) and Norovirus (Nv) are important etiological agents, yet data on their prevalence and determinants in North-central Nigeria are limited.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study involving 100 children under 5 years with acute diarrhoea was conducted at the Children’s Specialist Hospital, Ilorin, Kwara State between February to December, 2024.
analysis.methods: Virus detection was performed using qPCR, while a semi-structured questionnaire collected sociodemographic and environmental data. Associations were analyzed using chi-square tests and multivariable logistic regression.
analysis.main_results: Adenovirus prevalence was high (71%), while Norovirus GI and GII were detected in 4% and 12% of cases, respectively. Coinfection of Adv and Nv occurred in 13% of participants.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Adenovirus infection was significantly associated with sociodemographic and sanitation factors whereas no significant predictors were identified for Norovirus. Multivariable analysis showed sanitation-related factors as the strongest predictors.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings highlight key determinants of Adv and Nv infections in children under five, underscoring the need for targeted public health interventions among vulnerable populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study design limitations, including the cross-sectional nature and potential for residual confounding, limit the strength of the evidence. The sample size is relatively small, and the study is specific to a single location in North-central Nigeria, which may limit generalizability.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the prevalence and determinants of adenovirus and norovirus among children with acute diarrhea in Ilorin, Nigeria. Adenovirus was highly prevalent (71%), while norovirus was detected in 4% and 12% of cases for GI and GII, respectively. Sanitation-related factors were identified as key predictors, emphasizing the need for targeted public health interventions.

title: Human Norovirus GII is Widespread in the Coastal Marine Waters of the San Diego–Tijuana (US–Mexico) Border Region

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the presence and distribution of human norovirus GII in coastal marine waters of the San Diego–Tijuana border region, addressing the need to understand its environmental persistence and potential for transmission in this area.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A six-month ddPCR-based monitoring campaign was conducted in the Tijuana River Estuary and adjacent coastal ocean, focusing on sampling along a ∼12 km stretch of the US side of the coastal ocean border region from 19 June 2024 through 30 December 2024. Wastewater from Tijuana is collected by the South Bay International Wastewater Treatment Plant (SBIWTP), operated by the International Boundary Water Commission (IBWC), and carried downstream into the Tijuana Estuary and eventually to the coastal ocean.
analysis.methods: HuNoV GII concentrations were quantified using digital droplet PCR (ddPCR), with statistical analysis of spatial trends requiring per-sample analysis of the limit of blank (LoB). The study also evaluated sample recovery using a MuNoV spike and compared counts from GMM-based procedures with Bio-Rad QuantaSoft software.
analysis.main_results: From June to December 2024, average HuNoV concentrations varied across several orders of magnitude between sampling locations. The greatest average concentrations exceeded 105 copies L–1 at the shoreline location closest to the river mouth (PP-010), while other shoreline locations had mean values of approximately 104 copies L–1. Offshore locations had average values ranging from 102–103 copies L–1. The mean sample recovery from the MuNoV spike was 23.8 ± 5.3%, with no significant difference between samples collected at the river mouth and Silver Strand State Park Campground. Inhibition of RT-ddPCR was generally low, with only beach samples significantly different from the nuclease-free water control in the eluent fraction.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that HuNoV concentrations were highest at the river source and shoreline, decreasing with both cross-shore and along-shore distance. These spatial gradients align with expectations and previous physical models predicting wastewater discharge patterns in the region.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the environmental persistence of HuNoV GII in coastal waters and its potential for transmission in polluted areas, informing public health strategies for monitoring and mitigating viral spread in the San Diego–Tijuana border region.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the reliance on wastewater discharge data and the lack of continuous monitoring of the intermittent sources. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on a six-month monitoring campaign with spatial and temporal sampling, but the results are supported by statistical analysis and comparison with previous studies.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the spatial and temporal distribution of human norovirus GII (HuNoV GII) in the coastal marine waters of the San Diego–Tijuana border region. The research aimed to address the need for understanding HuNoV GII's environmental persistence and transmission risks in this area. A six-month ddPCR-based monitoring campaign was conducted in the Tijuana River Estuary and adjacent coastal ocean, focusing on a ∼12 km stretch of the US side. HuNoV GII concentrations were quantified using digital droplet PCR, with sample recovery evaluated using a MuNoV spike. Results showed that concentrations were highest at the river source and shoreline, decreasing with both cross-shore and along-shore distance. The study found that the mean sample recovery was 23.8 ± 5.3%, with no significant difference between river mouth and Silver Strand State Park samples. Inhibition of RT-ddPCR was generally low, with only beach samples significantly different from the nuclease-free water control. These findings align with physical models predicting wastewater discharge patterns in the region, highlighting the environmental persistence of HuNoV GII and its potential for transmission in coastal waters. title: IRF4 p.T95R combined immunodeficiency: Clinical features and transplant outcomes

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to characterize the clinical features and transplant outcomes of patients with IRF4 p.T95R combined immunodeficiency, a rare disorder associated with severe susceptibility to infections. The background highlights the need to understand the disease course and treatment outcomes in affected individuals.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed 10 patients with the IRF4 p.T95R variant, including four who underwent hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT). Patients spanned four continents, with disease onset uniformly early (<1 year) and a male predominance (8/10).
analysis.methods: Patients received HSCT with varying donor sources, conditioning regimens, and immunosuppression protocols. One patient had multiple HSCT donors, with the initial graft from a matched unrelated donor and subsequent grafts from the same mismatched related donor. Outcomes were evaluated based on survival and complications following transplant.
analysis.main_results: Two patients survived with a median follow-up of 37 months, while two died at 9 and 12.5 months post-HSCT. One death was due to multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae infection, and another was from thrombotic microangiopathy-associated multi-organ failure. Both patients had active infections (CMV and Cryptosporidium) at the time of transplant.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that IRF4 p.T95R combined immunodeficiency is characterized by marked susceptibility to a broad spectrum of infections, with HSCT outcomes being mixed. This study provides the most comprehensive description of the disorder to date.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the management of patients with IRF4 p.T95R combined immunodeficiency, particularly regarding the risks and outcomes of HSCT in the context of active infections. They also highlight the importance of early diagnosis and tailored immunosuppression strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective nature and the small sample size, which may affect the generalizability of the results. The evidence is moderate due to the lack of prospective data and the potential for unmeasured confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the clinical features and transplant outcomes of patients with IRF4 p.T95R combined immunodeficiency, a rare genetic disorder causing severe susceptibility to infections. Four of the 10 patients underwent hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), with mixed results: two survived, while two died from complications related to active infections at the time of transplant. The authors interpret that this condition is marked by broad immune dysfunction, with HSCT outcomes influenced by the presence of concurrent infections. The findings contribute to understanding the disease course and treatment challenges, emphasizing the need for careful management of infections in affected individuals. However, the study's retrospective design and small sample size limit the strength of the evidence, suggesting a moderate confidence level in the conclusions.

analysis.methods: The methods included targeted history-taking, chest CT imaging, bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) cytology, and next-generation sequencing of throat-swab and BALF samples. Klebsiella aerogenes was detected through these assays, and the patient's clinical course was documented.
analysis.main_results: Repeated targeted history-taking revealed multiple oral administrations of liquid paraffin with choking episodes. Chest CT showed bilateral consolidation, ground-glass opacities, interlobular septal thickening, a crazy-paving pattern, and a focal area of fat attenuation. BALF cytology showed vacuolated histiocytes, although lipid-specific staining was unavailable. The patient showed clinical and radiological improvement following discontinuation of paraffin exposure and multimodal management.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The case emphasizes that coughing or choking during administration of an oily medication to an infant should prompt immediate discontinuation, assessment of aspiration risk, and notification of medical personnel. It also highlights the importance of integrating exposure history, imaging, BALF findings, microbiological evidence, and clinical course for diagnosis.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the importance of detailed exposure history and early recognition of exogenous lipoid pneumonia in infants with treatment-refractory pneumonia and intralesional fat attenuation on CT. This can aid in timely intervention and improved patient outcomes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the concurrent administration of several interventions and the incomplete long-term follow-up, which prevents determining the efficacy of individual treatments and late pulmonary outcomes. The evidence is moderate due to the case report nature and lack of controlled comparisons.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a rare pediatric case of exogenous lipoid pneumonia (ELP) caused by repeated paraffin oil aspiration in a 4-month-old former preterm infant. The patient presented with severe pneumonia, and despite initial antimicrobial therapy, ELP was suspected based on clinical and radiological progression. The case highlights the importance of detailed exposure history, early recognition, and timely intervention in diagnosing ELP. Key findings included bilateral consolidation, ground-glass opacities, and vacuolated histiocytes in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF). Klebsiella aerogenes was detected through targeted next-generation sequencing and sputum culture, indicating a concomitant lower respiratory tract infection. The patient showed clinical and radiological improvement after discontinuation of paraffin exposure and multimodal management. The study underscores the need for integrating exposure history, imaging, BALF findings, microbiological evidence, and clinical course for accurate diagnosis. However, the concurrent use of multiple interventions and incomplete follow-up limit the ability to assess individual treatment efficacy and long-term outcomes. The evidence is moderate due to the case report format and the absence of controlled studies.
